trust_decision.summary: Per request, the proxy decides whether the OPA policy may treat the body it was given as complete: any body truncated to -open-policy-agent-max-request-body-size must reach the policy with truncated_body true, which is decided in the body reader that caps the stream and must be carried into the ext_authz CheckRequest headers.

landing_point.why: The summary says the truncated_body mitigation fails open on chunked/HTTP-2; the only place a body is read and capped is bufferedBodyReader.fillBuffer, and it throws away whether it stopped because it hit maxBufferSize, so an engineer looks here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: eskip filter opaAuthorizeRequestWithBody (route filter, registered at skipper.go:2318)
eskip filter opaServeResponseWithReqBody (route filter, registered at skipper.go:2320)
envoy.AdaptToExtAuthRequest, called by both body filters
fix_sites.module_kind: internal wrapper that composes the ext_authz CheckRequest

O3_reason_to_dismiss: opaServeResponseWithReqBody is a response-serving filter, not an access gate: it always renders the policy's response, so a truncated body there looks like it cannot bypass authorization and can be left unchanged.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An under-cap body, including a chunked/HTTP-2 request with no Content-Length, must still evaluate as not truncated and be allowed; a solver who marks every ContentLength<0 request truncated (or who rejects chunked bodies) breaks all legitimate streaming uploads, and one who flags any read that filled the buffer also denies a body of exactly the cap.

O6_input_shapes: oversized body with a known Content-Length (fillBuffer stops at maxBufferSize)
chunked Transfer-Encoding or HTTP/2 with no Content-Length (req.ContentLength == -1, driven with expectedSize = maxBodyBytes)
final read overshooting maxBodyBytes on the last chunk (rawBody sliced down, must be reported truncated)
under-cap body of either shape (must stay truncated=false)
no body, or skip-request-body-parse set (no read, flag false)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A request with a large body on a route using opaAuthorizeRequest or opaServeResponse (bodyParsing=false) is evaluated by the same OPA sink with an empty body and truncated_body=false; the fix now pins x-envoy-auth-partial-body to false for every filter without any body having been read.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Body parsing is opt-in: the docs point body-based policies at the WithBody filter, so a solver can call these routes a misconfiguration rather than an uncovered path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package tree, different filter package (filters/openpolicyagent/opaauthorizerequest) from the fixed filters

O8_uncovered_routes.route: With skip-request-body-parse enabled, ExtractHttpBodyOptionally returns before reading anything, so an oversized body reaches the same sink as no body at all with truncated_body=false.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A documented plugin option disables body parsing, so the solver can call it an unsupported combination that the policy author opted into.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, one branch earlier

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third body-carrying filter variant that copies this extract-then-adapt block but builds its CheckRequest without the partial-body signal.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The two body filters already duplicate the same six-line extraction and adapter call verbatim, so a maintainer adding another body filter would copy the block and re-introduce the gap.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second adapter (e.g. for the gRPC ext_authz server or a headers-only mode) that composes a CheckRequest and forgets the synthetic partial-body header.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The signal only exists because the plugin reads a header, not a proto field; any new constructor in internal/envoy must remember a convention that is invisible in the type.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second extraction API (ExtractHttpBody without the truncation output) used by a new caller.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The published fix changed this method's signature across all existing callers, so a sibling added later by copying an older call site would silently drop the flag.
